newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 18.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Savings deposit accounts are returning to single-digit interest rates after an 18-year hiatus, with the Credit Bank taking the lead with its announcement of a 9.5 percent interest rate on Friday. Other banks are expected to follow. However, despite developments, the difference between interest rates on deposits and lending remain great.

--Talks between Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, and US airline companies TWA and Continental on a commercial agreement are at an advanced stage. Sources at the airline said an agreement with either would be a coup for OA.
--The finance ministry has issued a guide to filling out the E9 declaration on real estate.
--The recent agreement on shop trading hours will be adopted by the government next week, despite disagreement from major supermarket chains.
--The mighty dollar continues its upward climb on international markets, monopolising the interest of investors. On the domestic market, the dollar marked a record increase to close at 265.070.
--Stock prices turned bullish on the Athens bourse yesterday with the general price index closing at 1,270.74 points, up 2.61 percent.
--The Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) yesterday called for greater flexibility in labour relations and a free hand in mass dismissals from the labour minister.
--Forty-two Northern Greek companies meet criteria to be listed on the Athens bourse, according to a new study.

--The government's move to transfer pension funds reserves to the Bank of Greece is an administrative measure, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou said yesterday. The Bank of Greece is to create a special mutual fund for the reserves to maximise returns.
--The Continent and Marinopoulos supermarket chains will seek recourse to the Council of State, the country's highest administrative court, over the issue of trading hours.

--Business sees the dream of participation in European Economic and Monetary Union slowly fading despite the right government policies and improving figures. The pace, the Athens Chamber said yesterday, is too slow.
--Labour Minister Miltiades Papaioannou pledged to examine SEB's demands on labour relations yesterday but said its call for freer hand in mass dismissals was not on the cards.

--European Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies will today present her ideas for speedier absorption of Community funds and the prompt completion of infrastructure projects, following her four-day visit to Athens. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
